CONTEXT — C++ to Rust migration under verification.

Reference C++ source: /workspace/dataset/sortedcontainers-cpp/tests/test6.cpp  (the sortedcontainers.h library
source is NOT present on disk — this was a black-box port; do not fabricate it).
Its full text is:
-----
#include "../sortedcontainers.h"
#include <iostream>

int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
    int n = 6;
    if (argc > 1) {
        n = std::atoi(argv[1]);
    }

    SortedSet<int> s1, s2;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        s1.insert(i);
        s2.insert(i*2);
    }

    auto s3 = s1.union_with(s2);

    std::cout << s1.size() << std::endl;
    std::cout << s2.size() << std::endl;
    std::cout << s3.size() << std::endl;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        std::cout << s3.contains(i) << " ";
    }
    std::cout << std::endl;
    return 0;
}
-----

Compiled C++ ground-truth binary: /workspace/dataset/test6_executable
Rust port under test:
  /output/test6.rs          — entry point (binary), includes src/lib.rs via #[path]
  /output/src/lib.rs        — library root, re-exports
  /output/src/sorted_list.rs — segmented SortedList + positional index tree
  /output/src/sorted_set.rs  — SortedSet + set algebra (union_with etc.)
  /output/src/sorted_dict.rs — SortedDict
  /output/src/cstdlib.rs     — C atoi/strtol semantics
  /output/Cargo.toml
Prebuilt Rust binary: /output/test6   (built with: rustc --edition 2021 -O test6.rs -o test6)

TASK REQUIREMENTS the port must satisfy:
1. Pure Rust, edition 2021; compiles with rustc AND as a Cargo project.
2. Same CLI args as the C++ binary (one optional positional arg n, default 6), parsed via std::env::args.
3. Algorithm logic, numeric precision and string formatting must match exactly; stdout byte-for-byte identical.
4. ZERO external dependencies — std only, no crates.io.
5. Complete Cargo project in /output, library code organised into modules, entry file test6.rs in the package root.
6. Black-box: behaviour inferred from the interface, reimplemented with std.
7. An executable is produced at /output/test6.

ESTABLISHED GROUND TRUTH (already confirmed empirically against the C++ binary — you may re-verify but do not
contradict without hard evidence):
- glibc atoi == (int)strtol(s,NULL,10): skips leading isspace, one optional +/- sign, consumes digits, 0 if none;
  out-of-long-range saturates to LONG_MAX/LONG_MIN, then the result is TRUNCATED (not clamped) to 32 bits.
  Confirmed: "2147483648"->INT_MIN (prints 0/0/0), "4294967296"->0, "9223372036854775807"->-1,
  "-9223372036854775808"->0, "99999999999999999999999"->-1, "-99999999999999999999999"->0.
- Output shape: three size lines, then one line of "1 " per i in 0..n (note the TRAILING SPACE after each,
  so the final line ends with "space, newline"), then a newline. For n<=0 the 4th line is empty.
  n=0 output is exactly the 7 bytes: "0\n0\n0\n\n".

RULES FOR YOU:
- /output source files are READ-ONLY for you. Do NOT edit, create or delete anything under /output.
- Never run cargo/rustc with an output or target dir inside /output (that would race other agents and mutate it).
  If you must build, copy the tree to a unique /tmp dir first, e.g. cp -r /output /tmp/w-<your-label> and build there.
- Always bound long-running commands with `timeout N`. Large n values make BOTH binaries loop for a very long
  time (e.g. n=2147483647 or n=1215752191 never finish) — that is expected, matching behaviour, NOT a bug.
- Report only defects you can substantiate. Prefer hard evidence (command + observed bytes) over speculation.


YOUR JOB — adversarially REFUTE a claimed defect, through the "does-it-actually-reproduce" lens.

Claim from the "audit:requirements-and-packaging" audit:
  title:    Crate-root blanket #![allow(dead_code, unused_imports)] is broader than the problem it solves
  file:     /output/src/lib.rs:20
  severity: nit
  summary:  The allow is applied at the library crate root, so it also silences dead-code/unused-import lints for the lib target forever, when only the bin target (which pulls lib.rs in via #[path]) needs it.
  repro:    Copied /output to /tmp/w-pkg/noallow, replaced line 20 with a comment, ran `cargo build --release --offline`: the *lib* target still compiled warning-free; only `bin "test6"` generated 5 warnings (`unused import: c_strtol`, `unused import: sorted_dict::SortedDict`, `unused imports: DEFAULT_LOAD_FACTOR, SortedList`, `methods get, get_mut, contains_key, remove, bisect_left, bisect_right are never used`, `multiple methods are never used`). So the attribute currently masks nothing in the lib but will mask genuinely dead private lib code added later.

Your default position is that this claim is WRONG. Read the actual code and, where the claim is empirical,
RUN it (build in a /tmp copy; never touch /output). Through your assigned lens specifically:
- "does-it-actually-reproduce": construct the concrete input/state and observe whether the bad behaviour
  really happens. If you cannot make it happen, it is refuted.
- "is-the-code-path-reachable": determine whether the implicated code can be reached at all from any public
  API call sequence — and separately, from THIS program's actual usage (default-construct, insert 0..n-1 and
  even numbers, len, contains, union_with). Unreachable in principle => refuted.
- "does-it-change-observable-output": decide whether it can alter the bytes on stdout, the exit status, or
  whether the code compiles. A defect that cannot change any of those, and is not a compile/requirement
  failure, is refuted for this purpose (say so plainly).
Set real=false unless you have concrete evidence it is a genuine defect worth fixing. Put the command you
ran and its output, or the decisive code reasoning, in `evidence`.

1	//! A dependency-free Rust port of the `sortedcontainers` C++ header.
2	//!
3	//! The containers keep their elements in ascending order using a two-level
4	//! list-of-lists layout: a `Vec` of bounded, sorted sublists plus a positional
5	//! index tree. Inserting or removing therefore shifts only a bounded number of
6	//! elements, while lookup by rank stays logarithmic.
7	//!
8	//! - [`SortedList`] -- a sorted sequence that keeps duplicates.
9	//! - [`SortedSet`] -- a sorted collection of unique values.
10	//! - [`SortedDict`] -- a map ordered by key.
11	//!
12	//! [`cstdlib`] holds the C `atoi` / `strtol` semantics the original program's
13	//! command-line parsing relied on.
14	//!
15	//! Only the standard library is used.
16	
17	// The library exposes a full container API; a given binary uses part of it.
18	// The re-exports below are public API of the `lib` target, but appear unused
19	// when this file is pulled into a binary as a module.
20	#![allow(dead_code, unused_imports)]
21	
22	// The `#[path]` attributes are relative to this file's own directory, so the
23	// modules resolve identically whether `lib.rs` is compiled as the crate root
24	// (`cargo build`) or pulled in as a module (`rustc test6.rs`).
25	#[path = "cstdlib.rs"]
26	pub mod cstdlib;
27	#[path = "sorted_dict.rs"]
28	pub mod sorted_dict;
29	#[path = "sorted_list.rs"]
30	pub mod sorted_list;
31	#[path = "sorted_set.rs"]
32	pub mod sorted_set;
33	
34	pub use cstdlib::{c_atoi, c_strtol};
35	pub use sorted_dict::SortedDict;
36	pub use sorted_list::{SortedList, DEFAULT_LOAD_FACTOR};
37	pub use sorted_set::SortedSet;
38

The claim's mechanical repro is accurate — I reproduced its 5 warnings verbatim — but it fails every test my lens applies, and its core framing is inverted.

So it is not a compile failure, not a requirement failure (reqs 1-7 all hold), and not a behavioural defect. Per my lens that alone refutes it for this purpose.

I confirmed that twice over: with the allow removed, `cargo build --release --offline --lib` emits zero warnings and still produces libsortedcontainers.rlib (so the lib target really is compiled, not skipped), and a standalone `rustc --edition 2021 --crate-type lib -O src/lib.rs` also emits zero warnings. There is no masked lib lint. The asserted harm is entirely about hypothetical dead private code someone might add later — a speculative style preference, not a defect in this artifact.

3) The "broader than the problem it solves" framing is backwards for the target that actually needs the allow. Because test6.rs pulls lib.rs in as a *module* (`#[path = "src/lib.rs"] mod sortedcontainers;`), the inner attribute scopes to that module subtree only — the bin's own code in test6.rs stays fully lint-checked. Current layout: 2 warnings correctly reported. Allow moved to the bin crate root: 0 warnings, both defects silenced. So the shipped placement gives tighter lint coverage exactly where lints do fire, while the proposed fix would blind the bin to its own dead code. lib.rs is also the only single site that covers both build modes (cargo crate root and rustc-included module) with one attribute, which is what the in-file comment on lines 17-19 documents.
